title: Best Post‑Workout Meals for NZ Gym‑Goers
meta_desc: Discover evidence‑based post‑workout meals using NZ ingredients, bust the protein window myth, and get quick, budget‑friendly options for busy Kiwis.
intro: After a hard training session you want to refuel efficiently without breaking the bank. This guide separates myth from science and gives you practical meal ideas using ingredients you can find at any NZ supermarket.

sections.heading: The protein synthesis window – myth or fact?
sections.body: Research shows that muscle protein synthesis stays elevated for up to 24 hours after resistance training, with the most noticeable rise in the first 2‑3 hours. The old “30‑minute window” is an oversimplification – you don’t need to eat immediately, just aim for a protein‑rich meal within a few hours. Consistency across the day matters more than exact timing, so focus on meeting your total daily protein target (1.6‑2.2 g per kg body weight for most active adults).

sections.heading: Key NZ protein sources on a budget
sections.body: New Zealand offers plenty of affordable, high‑quality protein options. Choose from these staples and keep an eye on supermarket flyers for specials.
list: Chicken breast – approx $8.00 kg⁻¹ at Countdown
Canned tuna (in spring water) – $1.50 per 95 g can at New World
Grass‑fed beef mince – $12.00 kg⁻¹ at The Warehouse
Whey protein isolate – $30.00 for 1 kg (bulk) from NZ‑sourced brands

sections.heading: Quick 30‑minute meals for the busy gym‑goer
sections.body: When time is tight, these meals can be assembled in half an hour or less, using ingredients you likely already have at home. Each provides around 20‑30 g of protein and a balanced mix of carbs and fats to support recovery.
list: Stir‑fried chicken strips with frozen mixed veg and instant brown rice – $3.20 per serving
Tuna & quinoa salad with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and a drizzle of olive oil – $2.80 per serving
Scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, spinach, and whole‑grain toast – $3.00 per serving
